mentions.note: went in front from the start of the senior race
beat Vic Blowfield up the finishing straight in the senior race
passed Verne Blowfield in the closing stages of the 1948 National C.C.
first Briton to break 14 minutes for three miles
won 1948 National; former 880 yards and 1 mile world record holder
won AAA 3 miles 1946 in British record 13:53.6
former world record holder for the mile
Blackheath's President; ran the 50th stage in 6:18; former world record holder mile and 880, A.A.A. mile 1935, European 1500m 1938 and 5000m 1946, National XC 1948
next broke the mile world record, at Motspur Park
won the mile at the British Games, June 1943

mentions.note: finished fifth in Belgrave v Blackheath at Wimbledon, 1941
won 1946 AAA 3 miles in British record 13:53.2; 5,000 metres at 1946 European Games, Oslo
won the 1948 National Cross Country at Graves Park, Sheffield
won Southern and English C.C. Championships 1948

mentions.h: BILL LUCAS "... a bold spirit in a loyal breast"
mentions.note: first Briton under 14 minutes for 3 miles

Sydney Wooderson congratulates Carter after the latter's inter-club win at Wimbledon, 1940.

FRONT COVER (The Times) A photo to bring back memories. The great SYDNEY WOODERSON, former world record holder for the mile, runs alongside Belgrave's Past-President and former international, TED STIMPSON during Blackheath Harriers' Centenary 100X1 mile relay at Croydon Arena. For full details of the occasion see page 13.
Blackheath's 31 year old Sydney Wooderson, a comparative novice at 3 miles, leads the Dutchman Willie Slykhuis on his way to victory in the 1946 AAA Championships in a British Record time of 13:53.2.
